items.speaker: Coach
items.text: After winning the gold medal, you gave interviews, featured in columns, and became renowned among arcanists.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: But so what?

items.speaker: Child
items.text: Mum, that's Charlotte's house! It's been so long since she—

items.speaker: Woman
items.text: Shh. Don't you go saying her name. She's a witch, understand?! A hag! It's written right there in her name!

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: No one is willing to speak your name. No one even dares walk past your house.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: Your garden no longer blooms. Only weeds sprout from the mud and dirt.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: So, then ...

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: Then, the war began.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: War?

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: That's right. You haven't seen it yet, but you will.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: Years ago, war destroyed your hometown, and you moved with your family to a new land.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: On the surface, it seemed like a safe place. You believed what everyone said, firmly convinced that there would be no fighting there.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: Isn't that a good thing?

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: I suppose you don't yet remember that day.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: That day?

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: Yes, that day.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: By modern measures, that day was far from a good one. The air was heavy with the stench of gunpowder after the military dropped bomb after bomb in the area, leaving debris and dust in their wake.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: But luckily, your house was untouched, and you managed to survive the war.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: Then what?

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: Look up.
The girl looks up. There is a shining golden sun before her. She gazes in disbelief, then rubs her eyes.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: How come I can see the sun in the training room?

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: You saw a similar sun in the sky on that day, too.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: That long-awaited peace seemed to finally be near. You hadn't heard the roaring of planes for a long while, and the desolate grasslands had started to show a hint of life.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: So, on that stretch of scorched earth, you began to dance.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: Eye of Day, Keeper of Balance. You are the Endless Well.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: Healing Sulis, shining Sulis, holy Sulis, to us, you tell.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: Do you remember the origins of the Floor Ritual?

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: Of course, I remember. Floor Rituals originate from ancient rituals. The shamans danced to avert strife, to implore Sulis's grace.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: It was originally a dance for peace.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: So you thought at that time.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: You saw the glorious sun, the soil turning from lifeless to fertile, the tender green sprouts breaking through the earth.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: That was the most successful dance of your life. For the first time, Sulis responded to your prayers. No one had ever done that at the Uluru Games before, not even you at your best.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: You heard that sharp whistling for the first time—that sound that still haunts you in every nightmare, like Arachne cursed to forever make her web.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: Soon, an incendiary bomb exploded beside you.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: So you lost your leg as a result. It seems that, in the end, the gods never favored you.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: Poor girl. Her beliefs have become a joke. If sacrificing everything yielded such results, it would be better if those so-called gods never even existed.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: And it has caused you never-ending pain. How can one who no longer believes in the gods ever receive their favor again?
She sneers mockingly.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: No. That's not true. Sulis is my friend.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: You poor little thing.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: Look at that medal hanging around your neck.
The girl lifts the medal to find a small dent in it.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: Do you remember how this dent got here?

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: This isn't my medal! My medal would never have a dent like this in it!

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: After you lost your leg, you threw your medal away as hard as you could, cursing through tears that you'd never set eyes on it again.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: Unfortunately, your curse didn't work.
There's a knock at the door.
Hello? Is anyone there?

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: Who is it?
Ms. Willow? I've got this week's snails!
The voice is unfamiliar.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: I'm here to say goodbye.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: Why?

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: My snails have arrived. If I don't open the door, that little scamp will be kept waiting.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: A minute, ten minutes, an hour ... That girl's mind is a mystery. Who knows how long she'll wait?

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: I need to answer the door.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: Will I see you again?

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: If it were possible, I'd hope you never do.
She shakes her head and reveals a helpless smile.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: But we will meet, Charlotte. Endings aren't always a matter of choice, nor can they be changed through will alone.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: Now, the time has come to say goodbye. Take good care of this medal, won't you? Don't take your anger out on it.
She makes her way out of the room.
Her movement is stiff and awkward, and her leg makes a strange scraping sound as she walks. Yet, still, she holds her neck high, like a black swan gliding on the water.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: *sigh*

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Ms. Willow, here are the snails for this week!
The jar of snails is taken by a thin, gloved hand.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Your payment's in the letterbox by the door.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: And ... thank you.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Wow, Ms. Willow! What was it you said just now? Did you say "thank you"?!

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I ain't never heard you say that word before! Are you sure you're Ms. Willow?
She places the snails on the table as usual, their soft heads gently emerging from their shells.
The weekly race begins, and after a long wait, the third snail is the first to reach the finish line.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: The victor is ... Number 3.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: You won.
She gathers the snail mucus and works it into a light yellow salve. This should suffice for the trip.
She prepares her luggage, reflecting on the many years since her last excursion.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Australia ... The sun is relentless there. I should probably bring a larger hat.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Still, I have a fair deal of lubricant remaining.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Oh, and there's this too.
She looks at the little box.
Within it lies the gleaming gold medal with the dent on one side.
Flowers, applause, cheers, lubricant, the golden sun, and a thousand shadows.
She gently kisses the dented edge of the medal.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Good night, my friend.
